question: How many formula units of CaSO₄ are attached to one molecule of water of crystallisation in Plaster of Paris?
solution:
The correct answer is** '__2__'. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Plaster of Paris is **calcium hemihydrate [CaSO4. 1/2 H2O]**
 
• The formula actually means that two molecules (or two formula units) of CaSO4 share one molecule of water so that the effective water of crystallization for** one CaSO****4 unit comes to half a molecule of water.**
 
• The formula of plaster of Paris can be written as **2CaSO4.H2O**
 
• On heating,2(CaSO4 .2H2O) -----> 2CaSO4 .H2O + 3 H2O
